subject.title: fix(msteams): add timeouts to SharePoint file send requests

question: Should OpenClaw adopt the proposed 30-second Graph control-plane deadline and 5-minute-plus-256-KiB/s SharePoint transfer deadline, and which overlapping PR should establish the shared timeout helper first?
rationale: The implementation is correct, but the timeout thresholds intentionally change delivery behavior for slow existing environments and two viable PRs currently modify the same policy owner.

options.title: Land file-consent policy first
options.body: Land https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/104120 as the shared timeout-policy owner, then rebase this PR and retain only its SharePoint graph-upload calls and distinct tests.

options.title: Land this PR first
options.body: Accept this PR as the shared timeout-policy owner, then rebase https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/104120 to reuse the helper without duplicating constants or tests.

options.title: Consolidate both paths
options.body: Pause both PRs and combine the two upload paths into one maintainer-owned change if the timeout policy should be reviewed and proven as a single delivery contract.

recommendation.title: Land file-consent policy first
recommendation.body: Land https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/104120 as the shared timeout-policy owner, then rebase this PR and retain only its SharePoint graph-upload calls and distinct tests.

likelyOwner.reason: This choice sets cross-path MS Teams delivery policy and landing order rather than requiring a mechanical contributor fix.
